access_links.label: Open Supply Hub map and facility search

access_note: Searching the map and contributing supplier lists are free; API integrations, custom exports and embedded maps are paid solutions.
description: Open Supply Hub is an open map and database of more than 2.5 million production facility locations in global supply chains, with facility names, addresses, sectors and the organisations that disclosed them, each matched to a persistent OS ID. It is run by Open Supply Hub, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, with contributions from over 4,000 brands, retailers, civil society groups and researchers. Coverage is global across apparel, electronics, automotive and other manufacturing sectors, with dense data for countries such as Bangladesh, India, Turkey, Vietnam and Brazil. Searching and exploring the map is free, and contributing supplier lists is free; API integrations, custom data exports and embedded maps are paid solutions, so the cost model is freemium. Caveats: the page read states no open data licence, only terms of service, and facilities are self-reported by contributors and matched by algorithm, so duplicates and stale sites may remain. For simulation it gives node locations for supply-chain network models, letting users overlay manufacturing sites with flood, earthquake or heat hazard layers and trace cascading failure from a disrupted region to buyers. It is related to the Panjiva and trade-flow records in this catalogue, which describe the shipments between such facilities.
